what_it_supports: RiC is the current ICA framework; RiC-CM 1.0 is the conceptual model, RiC-O 1.1 the recommended ontology implementation, and RiC-AG 0.1 the current application-guidance release.
conformance_boundary: Supports semantic alignment claims only; paleo-type does not currently claim formal RiC implementation/conformance.

standard_or_guidance: ICA Records in Contexts Conceptual Model
what_it_supports: Record resources, agents and activities are modelled as distinct contextual entities; RiC replaces the older four ICA description standards at conceptual-model level.
conformance_boundary: Useful reference for Source/context/agent/activity separation; local source granularity still requires archival judgement.

what_it_supports: Generic vocabulary for archival record resources, instantiations, agents and evidence-bearing relations; intended to describe any kind of archival record resource.
conformance_boundary: Local File is not asserted to be identical to rico:Instantiation in every case; any mapping must be explicit and loss-checked.

what_it_supports: TEI provides established distinctions for manuscript/source description, facsimile/sourceDoc/surface/zone/line, additions/deletions, abbreviation/expansion, original/regularized forms, responsibility, source and certainty.
conformance_boundary: Supports semantic/editorial separation; paleo-type does not currently claim TEI-XML conformance and should treat TEI as an export/interoperability target unless a migration is separately justified.

standard_or_guidance: DFG Code Guidelines for Safeguarding Good Research Practice
what_it_supports: Research-relevant information, methods, results and provenance must be documented in a discipline-appropriate and reconstructable way; research integrity and traceability are governing requirements.
conformance_boundary: General GWP framework; exact local data structures remain project/repository design choices.

standard_or_guidance: DFG Förderkriterien für wissenschaftliche Editionen in der Literaturwissenschaft
version_or_status: Edition criteria, edition 11/2015, still listed by DFG in 2026
what_it_supports: Requires established editorial standards, methodological distinction between Befund and Deutung, explication of historical Dokument versus abstracted Text, justified editorial guidelines/technical implementation and nachvollziehbare editorische Entscheidungen.
conformance_boundary: Funding/disciplinary guidance rather than a machine schema; strongly supports layer separation and explicit editorial reasoning.

what_it_supports: Standardized presentation of compound digital objects using resources such as Manifest, Canvas, Range and Annotation; suitable for interoperable image/page/region presentation.
conformance_boundary: Interoperability option only; no requirement to remodel the internal corpus around IIIF.

what_it_supports: Entity-Activity-Agent provenance can be represented and exchanged across systems; PROV can be specialized for domain-specific provenance.
conformance_boundary: External provenance interchange reference; no need for an internal RDF/PROV architecture unless a concrete interoperability requirement appears.
